Links: [{"title":"GitHub - Leoyang183/sync-agents-settings: Sync MCP server configs from Claude Code to Gemini CLI, Codex CLI, OpenCode, Kiro, and Cursor — one command, all agents. · GitHub","url":"https://github.com/Leoyang183/sync-agents-settings"},{"title":"GitHub - holstein13/mcp-config-manager: Manage MCP server configs across Claude, Gemini & other AI systems. Interactive CLI for server enable/disable, preset management & config sync. · GitHub","url":"https://github.com/holstein13/mcp-config-manager"},{"title":"mcp sync","url":"https://github.com/ejfn/mcp-sync"},{"title":"mcp sync","url":"https://github.com/EnjoyableWork/mcp-sync"},{"title":"mcp-sync 1.0.0","url":"https://docs.rs/crate/mcp-sync/latest/source/README.md"},{"title":"GitHub - Abdalkaderdev/mcpport: See, lint, sync and convert MCP server configs across Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and Cursor · GitHub","url":"https://github.com/Abdalkaderdev/mcpport"},{"title":"Crate mcp_sync","url":"https://docs.rs/mcp-sync/latest/mcp_sync"},{"title":"How to Add an MCP Server to Any AI Coding CLI (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Qwen, Oh My Pi)","url":"https://inventivehq.com/blog/add-mcp-server-to-ai-coding-cli"},{"title":"Claude Code Supercharged: Access Any AI Model via MCP Integration - lgallardo.com","url":"https://lgallardo.com/2025/09/06/claude-code-supercharged-mcp-integration/"},{"title":"GitHub - eggboy/mcpshare: Sync MCP servers to different coding agents · GitHub","url":"https://github.com/eggboy/mcpshare"}]

Several open-source tools already do this, and most treat Claude Code's config as the source of truth. I ran one search, so this is a sample rather than a full survey.

- **sync-agents-settings** (Leoyang183): reads MCP servers and CLAUDE.md instructions from Claude Code and pushes them to Gemini CLI, Codex CLI, Cursor, and about ten other tools. It also has `diff`, `doctor`, and `reconcile` commands for detecting drift. The README labels Claude Code as the single source of truth for MCP settings.
- **mcp-sync** (ejfn): uses an existing `~/.claude.json` or any Claude-format file as input. It copies servers into Gemini and Codex configs, with a `--prune` flag that removes servers absent from the source. Codex's config uses an mcp_servers key in TOML and only supports stdio servers.
- **mcp-sync** (Rust crate): takes a single canonical `mcp.yaml` and writes it out to Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and Antigravity, with a watch mode and dry-run option.
- **mcpport** (Abdalkaderdev): lists, lints, syncs, and converts configs across Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, and Cursor. It treats Claude Code local-scope servers as read-only sources.
- **mcpshare** (eggboy): syncs from a canonical `mcp.json` directory and preserves non-MCP settings in the Codex and Gemini files.
- **Format differences matter:** a guide notes that the protocol is portable; the config is not. Codex uses TOML while Claude and Gemini use JSON, and the HTTP field name differs (`url` vs. `httpUrl` for Gemini).

Two design choices come up across these tools: whether Claude Code or a neutral YAML/JSON file is the source, and whether to prune servers removed from the source or keep them in targets.

results:
Several open-source tools already do this, and most treat Claude Code's config as the source of truth. I ran one search, so this is a sample rather than a full survey.

- **sync-agents-settings** (Leoyang183): reads MCP servers and CLAUDE.md instructions from Claude Code and pushes them to Gemini CLI, Codex CLI, Cursor, and about ten other tools. It also has `diff`, `doctor`, and `reconcile` commands for detecting drift. The README labels Claude Code as the single source of truth for MCP settings.
- **mcp-sync** (ejfn): uses an existing `~/.claude.json` or any Claude-format file as input. It copies servers into Gemini and Codex configs, with a `--prune` flag that removes servers absent from the source. Codex's config uses an mcp_servers key in TOML and only supports stdio servers.
- **mcp-sync** (Rust crate): takes a single canonical `mcp.yaml` and writes it out to Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and Antigravity, with a watch mode and dry-run option.
- **mcpport** (Abdalkaderdev): lists, lints, syncs, and converts configs across Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, and Cursor. It treats Claude Code local-scope servers as read-only sources.
- **mcpshare** (eggboy): syncs from a canonical `mcp.json` directory and preserves non-MCP settings in the Codex and Gemini files.
- **Format differences matter:** a guide notes that the protocol is portable; the config is not. Codex uses TOML while Claude and Gemini use JSON, and the HTTP field name differs (`url` vs. `httpUrl` for Gemini).

Two design choices come up across these tools: whether Claude Code or a neutral YAML/JSON file is the source, and whether to prune servers removed from the source or keep them in targets.

content.content:
**Install**
- Claude Code plugin: `claude plugin marketplace add Leoyang183/sync-agents-settings`, then `claude plugin install sync-agents-settings`
- CLI without installing: `npx sync-agents-settings list`
- Global install: `npm install -g sync-agents-settings`, then run `sync-agents`

**Usage commands**
- `sync` (use `--dry-run` to preview), `list`, `diff`, `doctor`, `validate`, `reconcile`
- `sync-instructions` syncs CLAUDE.md to other agents' instruction files
- `--target` selects specific agents, and `--report json` gives CI-friendly output

**Supported targets (MCP sync)**
Gemini CLI, Codex CLI, OpenCode, Kiro CLI, Cursor, Kimi CLI, Vibe CLI (Mistral), Qwen Code, Amp, Cline CLI, and Windsurf. Aider is supported for instruction sync only.

**Source of truth**
Claude Code. The tool reads `~/.claude.json` and enabled plugin `.mcp.json` files.

**Preserves other settings?**
Yes, according to the examples. Existing settings such as a Gemini `theme` or an OpenCode `model` are kept. The README also says "Existing servers are never overwritten," so re-running is safe.

**Backups and dry-run**
- Yes to both. Sync backs up affected config files to `~/.sync-agents-backup/<timestamp>/` by default. `--no-backup` skips this.
- `--dry-run` previews changes without writing any files.

**License**
MIT.

content.content:
**Install:** `npx mcpport <command>` or `npm i -g mcpport`. It requires Node 22+.

**Sync usage:** The page shows `npx mcpport sync claude cursor` and `--apply` for writing. The syntax is `sync <from> <to>`, so Codex and Gemini CLI targets should work the same way (e.g., `npx mcpport sync claude codex --apply`), though the page shows no examples for those targets.

**Preserves other settings?** Yes, mostly:
- JSON files keep keys unrelated to MCP servers.
- Codex TOML keeps comments and unrelated tables.
- `~/.claude.json` keeps non-MCP keys and CRLF line endings, but is rewritten with 2-space indentation.
- Gemini CLI JSON files containing comments are read but never written, to avoid losing them.

**Backups:** Yes. The target file is copied to `<file>.<timestamp>.bak` before any write, and writes go through a temp file and rename. A target that fails to parse is never written.

**Dry run:** Yes. `sync` is a dry run unless `--apply` is passed. Conflicting servers are skipped unless `--force` is passed.

**Source of truth:** The page doesn't name one. mcpport has no config file of its own. It reads each agent's native config (user and project scope) and normalizes it internally. Claude Code's format is used as the reference in the translation table.

**License:** MIT.

**Last activity:** The page doesn't show a date for the last commit. It lists 14 commits and links to the Activity tab, but the date column is blank in the captured content. You'd need to check the Activity page directly.

content.content:
**Install**
- From GitHub: `uv tool install git+https://github.com/eggboy/mcpshare.git`
- From a local clone: `uv tool install .`
- Upgrade: `uv tool upgrade mcpshare`

**Usage commands**
- `mcpshare init`: creates the config file and master directory.
- `mcpshare pull`: collects server entries from the `init-source` tools into the master `mcp.json`. It does not write to targets.
- `mcpshare sync`: writes the master to every configured target in each tool's native format.
- `mcpshare status`: shows master servers, the `init-source` list, target file existence, and disabled lists.
- `mcpshare disable` / `mcpshare enable --servers <name> [--ide <tool>]`: manage disabled servers.

**Supported agents**
Yes, Gemini CLI is supported, along with Claude Code and Codex. The page also lists VSCode, GitHub Copilot CLI, Google Antigravity, and OpenCode.

**Source of truth**
- The master `mcp.json` lives in the `source` directory set in `~/.config/mcpshare/config.yaml`.
- Disable state lives in `mcp.disabled.yaml`, next to the master `mcp.json`. It is a flat mapping: `"*"` applies to every IDE, and tool names (e.g., `claude`, `codex`) list servers disabled for that tool only.

**Preserves other settings?**
Yes. `sync` replaces only the MCP servers section, leaving unrelated keys alone. Examples include VSCode's `inputs`, Claude's state in `~/.claude.json`, Gemini and OpenCode settings, and non-MCP Codex TOML sections. Writes are atomic, follow symlinks, and keep file permissions. Malformed JSON or TOML targets are skipped, not overwritten.

**Backups / dry-run**
The page doesn't mention either feature.

**License**
The page doesn't show a license.

content.text:
## My recommendation: **sync-agents-settings** (free, MIT, local, no account)

It fits your setup best: you keep adding servers in Claude Code the usual way (`claude mcp add …`), and the tool copies them into Codex CLI's TOML and Gemini CLI's JSON. It also has the safety features you want:
- **`--dry-run`** shows what would change without writing anything.
- **Automatic backups** of each file it touches go to `~/.sync-agents-backup/<timestamp>/`.
- **Other settings are left alone.** The README's examples show unrelated keys like Gemini's `theme` being kept, and it says existing servers are never overwritten, so running it again is safe.
- **`diff`, `doctor` and `reconcile`** let you catch differences between the three configs later.

**My assumption:** you're happy for Claude Code to hold the master list, since you already use it. If you'd rather have a neutral master file that no agent owns, see mcpshare below.

### Install (macOS, needs Node.js)
```bash
# Try it without installing:
npx sync-agents-settings list

# Or install globally:
npm install -g sync-agents-settings
```

### First run
```bash
# 0. (Optional but wise) make your own copies first
cp ~/.claude.json ~/.claude.json.manual-bak
cp ~/.codex/config.toml ~/.codex/config.toml.manual-bak
cp ~/.gemini/settings.json ~/.gemini/settings.json.manual-bak

sync-agents list                 # list the MCP servers it found in Claude Code
sync-agents diff                 # compare against Codex and Gemini
sync-agents sync --dry-run       # preview the changes
sync-agents sync                 # write them (backups are made automatically)
```
You can limit a sync to certain agents with `--target`; check `sync-agents --help` for the exact target names. After syncing, run `/mcp` inside Gemini CLI and Codex to confirm the servers appear.

From then on: `claude mcp add …` → `sync-agents sync`.

**One thing to watch:** since it never overwrites existing servers, editing or removing a server in Claude Code may not carry over automatically. Check whether `reconcile` handles that before you depend on it.

## Alternatives
- **mcpshare** (`uv tool install git+https://github.com/eggboy/mcpshare.git`). This is the closest to "one list, synced everywhere": you keep a master `mcp.json` and run `mcpshare init` → `mcpshare pull` (imports your existing servers) → `mcpshare sync`. It only replaces the MCP section of each file, skips target files it can't parse instead of overwriting them, and can turn servers off for individual agents. The downsides: its README mentions no dry-run or backups, and I couldn't see a license.
- **mcpport** (`npx mcpport sync claude codex`, needs Node 22+, MIT). It reads each agent's own config with no master file. Syncs are dry runs unless you add `--apply`, it makes timestamped `.bak` files, and it keeps comments in Codex's TOML. One catch: it won't write Gemini settings files that contain comments.
- **mcp-sync** (Rust crate): uses a canonical `mcp.yaml` and has watch and dry-run modes. Check that its Gemini support covers what you need.

## What I checked
I didn't install or test any of these. Pickfit (a catalog of tools it has test-installed) had nothing that does this job, so these come from a web search and the projects' READMEs. Because the tools are small, young projects, back up your configs and do a dry run first. Codex only supports some server types, and Gemini names the remote-URL field differently (`httpUrl` instead of `url`), so check those settings after your first sync.

Sources:
- [sync-agents-settings](https://github.com/Leoyang183/sync-agents-settings)
- [mcpshare](https://github.com/eggboy/mcpshare)
- [mcpport](https://github.com/Abdalkaderdev/mcpport)
- [mcp-sync (Rust)](https://docs.rs/crate/mcp-sync/latest/source/README.md)
- [mcp-sync (ejfn)](https://github.com/ejfn/mcp-sync)
- [mcp-config-manager](https://github.com/holstein13/mcp-config-manager)
- [Adding MCP servers to each CLI (format differences)](https://inventivehq.com/blog/add-mcp-server-to-ai-coding-cli)
